problems.title: Which traversal?

parts.prompt: The values of a BST in sorted order:
The leftmost node of every level:
Serialise a tree to rebuild it later:

problems.solution: In-order sorts a BST, BFS gives levels, and pre-order with nulls is unambiguous.

problems.title: Traversal sequences
hints: Node, left, right / left, node, right / left, right, node.

problems.title: Is it a BST?
hints: Check each node against all its ancestors.
problems.solution: [5, 4, 6, ., ., 3, 7] puts 3 in 5's right subtree. [1, 1] has a duplicate.

problems.title: LCA
hints: A node can be its own ancestor.
problems.solution: 7 and 4 are children of 2; 6 and 4 split at 5; 5 is an ancestor of 4; 7 and 8 split at the root 3.

problems.title: BST LCA
problems.statement: In a BST, what is the rule for walking down to LCA(p, q)?

options: If both are smaller go left, if both are larger go right, otherwise this node is the LCA
Search for p, then search for q, then compare paths only

hints: The first node that separates them.
problems.solution: The LCA is the first node whose value lies between p and q (inclusive): O(h).

problems.title: Ambiguity

parts.prompt: Does the in-order sequence alone determine the tree?
options: No: [1, 2] as a left chain and as a right chain can share it

problems.solution: Root 2 with left child 1, and root 1 with right child 2, both have in-order 1 2. Pre-order picks the root, and in-order splits the subtrees.

problems.title: Building cost
problems.statement: Building a tree from pre-order and in-order (n nodes).

parts.prompt: Searching for the root in the in-order slice each time costs, in the worst case…
With a hash map from value to in-order index…

hints: A skewed tree makes the linear search repeat.
problems.solution: The hash map makes each root lookup O(1); passing index ranges instead of list slices avoids copying.

problems.title: k-th smallest

parts.prompt: With the iterative in-order, how many nodes have been popped when it returns?

problems.solution: The third value in sorted order is 3. The iterative traversal stops after 3 pops, so it costs O(h + k).

problems.title: Successor
problems.statement: In a BST, the in-order successor of a node x…

parts.prompt: If x has a right subtree:
options: the leftmost node of that right subtree
the last node where you went left

hints: Successor = the smallest value greater than x.
problems.solution: Both cases follow from the BST range property; each costs O(h).
